subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <samir.joshi@finpay.com>, Emily Tan <e.tan@finpay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-16T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Hi Samir / Emily —

Thanks again for the call today — great context. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can move toward a PoC decision: 

Summary of requirements (as I captured them)
- Product: real-time chat + occasional long-form generation for reporting
- P95 latency target (user-facing chat): <= 150 ms (ideal: ~100 ms)
- Baseline traffic: ~600 requests/sec; peak/spike traffic up to ~1,200 req/sec during promotions
- Typical tokens per request: 40–80 tokens (chat), occasional batch jobs 1k–2k tokens
- Hard constraint: consistent p95 during spikes (low variance)

Initial recommendation
- Hosted API: fastest path to prod, good for validation and lower-concurrency workloads. However, under sustained high concurrency (800+ rps) you'll see higher latency variance and potential throttling during bursts.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended for FinPay given the sustained baseline + high spikes. Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools (predictable throughput), lower latency variance, and the ability to tune batching/kv-cache for your workloads.

Suggested next steps
1) Share a short traffic/profile sample (I attached finpay_qps_profile.csv) — we'll use this to run a 1-hour synthetic load on Hosted and a short Dedicated trial.
2) Dylan (cc) will propose a PoC config and target capacity (expected: 4 GPU equivalent pool to start).
3) We'll provide ballpark pricing for a 2-week Dedicated PoC vs Hosted per-token estimate for your current profile.
4) If PoC looks good, we'll prep a short PoC MSA and provisioning timeline.

Attachments: [Attachment: finpay_qps_profile.csv]

If that summary looks right, I'll schedule the PoC kickoff for the week of 4/25 and loop in our infra engineer for capacity provisioning.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-16T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Thanks Neha — this is helpful and matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- P95 target: 100 ms would be ideal, 150 ms is our absolute upper bound for the user chat experience.
- Spike behaviour: spikes to ~1,200 rps are short (5–15 minutes) but frequent (a few times per week).
- Cost sensitivity: we prefer minimizing fixed monthly commitments but will consider Dedicated if the performance delta justifies it.

Two asks before we schedule the PoC:
1) Can you provide a ballpark monthly cost for the Dedicated configuration you're proposing (4 GPU-equivalent pool) vs Hosted for our profile? Even a rough number helps with procurement.
2) Can we run a Hosted stress test first to see how much variance we observe, or do you recommend jumping straight to Dedicated?

Appreciate the attachment — I'll send a representative qps dump by EOD if helpful.

—Samir

Head of Platform, FinPay

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-17T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Neha / Marcus —

Quick technical take after reviewing the requirements and the qps profile:

Why Dedicated makes sense for FinPay
- Predictable concurrency: With 600 baseline / 1,200 spike profile, you'll hit contention on shared-hosted pools that increases p95 variance. Dedicated lets us reserve capacity and control batch windows.
- Latency variance: On Hosted we typically see median latencies in the 60–90 ms range for 40–80 token requests, but p95 can drift above 150 ms under sustained bursts. Dedicated reduces tail latency by removing noisy neighbors and allowing more aggressive KV-cache and batching policies.
- Autoscaling and failover: We can configure autoscaling thresholds and warm standby capacity for short spikes to avoid cold starts.

Suggested PoC config (initial)
- Reserved pool: equivalent of 4 H100 GPUs (can be adjusted after initial runs)
- Concurrency profile: target sustained 800 rps with ability to absorb 1,500 rps short spikes
- Runtime config: favor lower batching for chat (to hit p95 targets) and enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts
- Monitoring: token-level latency + per-route p50/p95, throughput, and error rates; keep sampling for qualitative output checks

I’ll prepare a short PoC config doc and a lightweight load harness we can run against Hosted first (1-hour stress) and then the Dedicated pool. Attaching the PoC config PDF for your review.

Attachments: [Attachment: poc-configuration-proposal.pdf]

If you want, I can run the Hosted stress test next Tuesday (4/20) and share the results the same day. Dedicated trial can be ready within 48 hours of sign-off.

—Dylan

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Samir — thanks for the quick reply and for the clarity on targets. Proposed next steps based on Dylan’s assessment: 

1) Hosted stress test (optional first step)
- We can run a 1-hour Hosted stress test using the attached qps profile on 4/20. This will show tail behavior under bursts. No commitment required; gives us a baseline.

2) Dedicated 2-week PoC (recommended)
- Start week of 4/25. We’ll provision a 4-GPU equivalent pool for 2 weeks, run your traffic profile, and iterate on batching/cache settings.
- Ballpark pricing for PoC: $18,000–$24,000 for the 2-week reserved trial (includes reserved GPU capacity + engineering support). Post-PoC committed pricing will be scoped based on final capacity and run-rate.

3) Logistics
- Can you confirm which you prefer (Hosted stress test first, or go straight to Dedicated PoC)?
- If PoC: please review the short PoC MSA (I’ll send DocuSign once you confirm) and share any procurement contacts we should loop in.

I’ll put a calendar hold for the PoC kickoff on 4/25 and schedule Dylan to run the initial tests.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
